output.summary: An annual or biennial mustard-family herb native to much of North America and Central America. Its branched flower clusters resemble bottlebrushes, bearing small white flowers followed by greenish fruits. Young leaves are eaten raw or cooked, while young seedpods serve as a black-pepper substitute.
output.edibilityNote: Young leaves are eaten raw, sautéed or as a cooked green; young seedpods are used as a black-pepper substitute.
